text: We evaluated early stopping on weak-label validation loss (patience of 1) in a weak-to-strong generalization setup, with gpt2-large as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across 8 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.64 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.84, while the strong student trained on weak labels attained a transfer accuracy of 0.69 (SE 0.02). The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.23 (SE 0.08), which is identical to the baseline PGR of 0.23. This provides no evidence that early stopping on weak-label validation loss recovers additional performance gap relative to the baseline; the difference is zero and well within the margin implied by the PGR standard error of 0.08. The relatively large PGR standard error, combined with the modest seed count, means that even moderately sized effects in either direction would be difficult to detect here, so these numbers should be read as inconclusive rather than as a demonstration of equivalence.
